hook: Write down a local news report by ear and catch the moment the neutral press voice turns into a quoted, angry resident.
intro: Twelve sentences of one local news report, dictated: a new footbridge that was ceremonially opened but stays closed. The report is written in the neutral press register, and it breaks that register twice with quoted residents — „Die Brücke ist doch ein Witz“ and „Die haben uns jahrelang was vom Pferd erzählt“ — so you must supply the Anführungszeichen and the comma after the closing quote. Four sentences report official positions in the Konjunktiv I: man habe die Mängel erst bei der Abnahme festgestellt · der Zeitplan sei durchaus ehrgeizig gewesen · das ohnehin absehbar gewesen sei · Man werde die Brücke noch vor dem Winter freigeben. Four gradation adverbs carry the evaluation: durchaus, keineswegs (Die Anwohner sehen die Sache keineswegs so gelassen), geradezu (Die Kosten sind seit Baubeginn geradezu explodiert) and ohnehin. One allusion — an des Kaisers neue Kleider erinnert (the fairy tale of the emperor’s new clothes) — and one closing understatement, Ein Vorzeigeprojekt sieht anders aus, complete the text. Type each sentence whole; punctuation is part of the task.
tips[0].title: Hear the quotation marks
tips[0].text: When the register drops — doch, ein Witz, die for ‘they’, was for etwas, an idiom like jemandem was vom Pferd erzählen — the reporter is quoting. German opens low („) and closes high (“); the comma comes after the closing mark, before the verb of saying.
tips[0].trap: The comma goes outside the closing quotation mark: „…“, sagt sie — never „…,“ sagt sie.
tips[0].check.why: German quotes open low and close high, and the comma comes after the closing mark, before the verb of saying.
tips[1].title: Report → Konjunktiv I
tips[1].text: After erklären, einräumen, sprechen von, zurückweisen, the official voice is reported in the Konjunktiv I: habe, sei, werde. The ending is often a single syllable — listen for habe (not hat), sei (not ist), werde (not wird).
tips[1].check.why: After einräumen the press register reports in the Konjunktiv I: sie habe, not the indicative hat.
tips[1].visual.rows[0].b: Das sei eine Frechheit, sagte ein Anwohner.
tips[2].title: Gradation adverbs: the evaluation is in one word
tips[2].text: durchaus (certainly — often concessive after einräumen) · keineswegs (by no means) · geradezu (downright, all but) · ohnehin (anyway, in any case). They are unstressed in fast speech; if the sentence sounds oddly flat, an adverb is probably hiding in it.
tips[2].check.why: durchaus is the conceding 'certainly' that typically follows einräumen; keineswegs would deny the point.
tips[3].title: Allusion and understatement close the report
tips[3].text: The allusion keeps its old genitive word order — des Kaisers neue Kleider, not die neuen Kleider des Kaisers. The last line judges by understatement: it does not say ‘failure’, it says what a flagship project would look like.
tips[3].check.why: Understatement does not name the failure; it says what the project was not, and the reader draws the conclusion.
remember[0]: Register drop → quotation marks „…“, comma after the closing mark.
remember[1]: Reported official voice → habe / sei / werde.
remember[2]: durchaus · keineswegs · geradezu · ohnehin: hear the whole adverb.
remember[3]: des Kaisers neue Kleider: the allusion keeps its fixed wording.
exam: Taking down a press report exactly, quotation marks and all, is C2 exam material — and what you do when you minute a meeting or quote a source.
